stem.en: Kabir asks whether a bilayer bubble "leaks". He drops salt into the water outside one in the sim; it does not get in. He drops a little oil-loving dye; it slides straight through. Why?

text.en: The bubble's middle is two oily tails thick. Anything oily can dissolve in it and cross. A charged ion cannot enter an oily layer, from III.5, so salt stays out.
The bubble has holes just the size of dye.

feedback.en: There are no holes. The dye dissolves into the oily middle and out the other side, the way wax dissolves in oil.
Ions are tiny. What stops them is charge: an ion with its water shell cannot enter oil.

text.en: The bubble is closed, so nothing gets in.

feedback.en: The dye got in. The wall is choosy, not sealed, and the choosing is by oiliness.

explanation.en: The wall's middle is oil. Ask of anything: can it dissolve in oil? Oil-lovers pass. Charges are stopped.
